gap: No result ChatGPT got puts the plug-in inverters on the same footing for a two-panel 120 V setup: one APsystems EZ1-LV gives 900 VA, which works out to 7.5 A, for $325, while two Hoymiles HiFlow 360 Pro LV units give 720 VA, or 6.0 A, for $320.84. That is 25% more AC ceiling for about the same money. And EcoFlow's '1,200 W' is a cap on the whole STREAM system's grid output, not a figure that adds up per unit.
standout_why: I opened Solar Waypoint (cited), pluginsolarcheck.com/kits/certifications (cited) and the APsystems EZ1 product page (cited). Solar Waypoint lists VA ratings and prices in separate columns (Hoymiles $149/$169, EZ1-LV $325/$275) but never works out cost per VA, cost per panel, or amps at 120 V. It also never compares one dual-input EZ1-LV against two single-input Hoymiles units. It does say the EcoFlow STREAM is '800 W one unit; up to 1,200 W in supported combinations', so my EcoFlow finding only partly overlaps. Pluginsolarcheck gives the EZ1-LV as '900 W' and the EcoFlow STREAM Microinverter as '1,200 W' with no amps and no system-cap context. Neither page sets the CSA certificate's 'dedicated 10 A circuit' condition, which both report, against APsystems' own '1,800 W on a standard 15 A circuit' line. I did not open howtogosolar.org, plugshine.com, balconysolarkits.us, solar.com, promptquorum.com, balconysunlab.com or pluginsolarcalcs.com, so one of them might already have a per-VA comparison.
decides: This backs ChatGPT's EZ1-LV pick, with a reason it didn't give. For two panels, the EZ1-LV costs about the same as two Hoymiles 360 Pro LV units but has 180 VA more ceiling, so two 400 W panels (800 W DC) don't clip on it. Two 400 W panels would clip at 360 VA each on the Hoymiles. The Hoymiles stays the pick only for a single-panel setup or a state with a low wattage tier (Solar Waypoint reports Maine at 420 W and Colorado/Maryland around 391 W). It also undercuts ChatGPT's 'EcoFlow up to 1,200W' card: on EcoFlow's own page, 1,200 W is the most the STREAM system can feed to the grid in any configuration, and the microinverter adds solar input to a STREAM Ultra. EcoFlow's page doesn't say the microinverter can feed a wall outlet on its own.

findings.label: Max continuous AC output
findings.value: 900 VA (installer page says '900W maximum continuous output')
findings.note: Product page: 'Max output power reaching 900VA'. The installer page https://usa.apsystems.com/ez1-installers/ FAQ says 'rated for 900W maximum continuous output'.

findings.label: AC output current at 120 V (calculated)
findings.note: 900 VA ÷ 120 V = 7.5 A. A continuous load sized at 125% needs 9.4 A, which fits the 10 A dedicated breaker that Solar Waypoint and pluginsolarcheck report from CSA certificate 80310017.

findings.label: DC input per channel
findings.value: 2 independent MPPT channels, modules 315 W to 660 W+ each; 18 A input current and 25 A short-circuit current per input; MPPT 27–45 V; max input 60 V
findings.source_title: Turn Portable Solar Into New Business - APsystems USA
findings.note: The module range is from the FAQ text. The current and voltage figures are from the datasheet image caption on the same page.

findings.label: Price, maker US store
findings.source_title: Turn Portable Solar Into New Business - APsystems USA
findings.note: $325 ÷ 900 VA = $0.361 per VA. $325 ÷ 2 panels = $162.50 per panel. Solar Waypoint (2026-11-03) reported it sold out direct.

findings.label: Maker's two-unit claim vs certificate condition
findings.value: Maker says two EZ1s give 'up to 1,800W of plug-in solar power on a standard 15A circuit'. The CSA certificate condition, as rivals report it, is a dedicated 10 A circuit.
findings.source_title: Turn Portable Solar Into New Business - APsystems USA
findings.note: The 1,800 W line is in a YouTube video description on the APsystems page, not the datasheet. 2 × 7.5 A = 15 A, which is 100% of a 15 A breaker before any 125% continuous factor. I did not open the CSA certificate myself; the condition comes from solarwaypoint.com and pluginsolarcheck.com.

findings.label: Output limit setting
findings.value: Max output adjustable in the AP EasyPower app (no range stated)
findings.source_title: Turn Portable Solar Into New Business - APsystems USA
findings.note: The page says 'Adjustable output helps meet local system requirements'. Zero-export needs the optional APmeter ($90) per the product page.

findings.label: Rated AC output and module range per model
findings.note: Hoymiles labels this 'rated output power', not 'max continuous'. At 120 V: 3.0 / 3.26 / 3.5 / 3.75 / 4.17 A (calculated). The page lists max input voltage as 64 V; the solar-electric.com listing says 60 V.

findings.label: Price and electrical detail, US retailer
findings.value: $160.42; rated output 360 VA, rated output current 3.0 A, power factor >0.99 default (adjustable 0.8 leading–0.8 lagging), efficiency 95.50%, night consumption <50 mW, UL 1741 / UL 3700 / IEEE 1547 (listed)
findings.source_title: Hoymiles HMS-360-1WM-LV HiFlow Pro LV 1-in-1 series plug-in microinverter - Northern Arizona Wind & Sun
findings.note: $160.42 ÷ 360 VA = $0.446 per VA, 23% more than the EZ1-LV's $0.361. Two units for two panels: 720 VA for $320.84, against one EZ1-LV at 900 VA for $325.00. Because the default power factor is >0.99, VA and W are effectively equal for both makers.

findings.label: What '1,200 W' means
findings.value: STREAM Ultra alone: max 800 W on-grid AC. Ultra + one STREAM Microinverter: max 1,200 W on-grid AC. 2 to 6 Ultra units: still max 1,200 W on-grid. The microinverter adds 'an additional 1,200W of solar input'.
findings.source_title: EcoFlow STREAM Ultra Home Solar System - EcoFlow US
findings.note: 1,200 W is a whole-system grid-output cap (10 A at 120 V, calculated), not a per-unit rating that stacks. The page lists UL1741 and IEEE1547 but not UL 3700, and doesn't say whether the microinverter feeds an outlet on its own.

findings.label: Published output rating
findings.value: Spec table is labelled BDM 800: rated AC output 800 W, rated output current 3.2 / 3.36 / 3.26 A, 2 inputs at 17 A each, MPPT 22–55 V, CEC weighted 95.50%, recommended max PV 1,200 W; UL 1741 and CSA C22.2 No. 107.1 listed, UL 3700 not mentioned
findings.note: The product is named 1200, but the table on the page is for the BDM 800, so its 1,200 W AC output is not shown there. The listed currents don't match 800 W at 120 V, so the table looks wrong. No price on the page.
